requiredNativePairedGroups.cases: Both TimeSpan overloads across pending/success/fault/cancel source and None/live/precanceled caller: invalid -2ms, MinValue, MaxValue and max+1ms throw synchronously even when source complete or caller canceled. Exact ticks around -2ms,-1ms,0,+1ms,max,max+1ms establish truncation; valid max never requires waiting days. Assert timeout ParamName, type/message/HResult and zero resource demand for synchronous refusals via private complement.

All three overloads: completed success/fault/cancel retain original identity for valid zero/finite/infinite and all token states; pending infinite+None retains original; pending canceled caller beats zero and returns distinct canceled task; pending zero/live or None gives distinct faulted timeout task. Assert original status remains independent.

Each applicable overload and each original terminal kind: original success, original single fault (including AggregateException-as-one-fault and faulted OCE), original cancellation, caller cancellation, finite timeout. Use explicit gates for ordered native outcomes; record initial WaitingForActivation, terminal predicates, Exception/null, original fault identity, GetResult, cancellation-token equality and Task identity. Do not require nondeterministic timing winner or exact milliseconds.

Inspect new TaskCanceledException(task) on original and returned task while pending and after success/fault/cancel/timeout. Cover TCS.SetCanceled(None/live/requested token), FromCanceled, Delay, Run(Action), Run(Action,token) success/fault/requested matching OCE, and CTS.CancelAsync-returned tasks. Fast-path aliases retain Run association; newly created success/fault/timeout wrappers keep None. Source-canceled wrapper copies token and stored original OCE identity where present; otherwise GetResult synthesizes TCE naming wrapper, without requiring repeated synthesized exception identity. Caller-canceled wrapper uses caller token, distinct from source token. Include disposed source/token and nested waits.

Two waits on one source with different caller tokens/deadlines; cancel/timeout one while other completes from original. After a wait loses, independently complete/fault/cancel original and inspect original consumers. Cancel caller token after source won. Dispose caller/source CTS before and after attachment according to existing registration semantics; no implicit CTS disposal/cancellation.

Mixed original await callbacks and one/two wait completion actions in both registration orders, duplicate user Actions, reentrant late registrations, blocked first callback and independently scheduled later callbacks; compare only source-supported default-context order/inline facets. Caller-cancellation wrapper first callback may run inline within Cancel, unlike Delay cancellation. Canceled Delay source queues its wait action; downstream wrapper retains its own normal policy. Native callback exceptions that would terminate process belong to private controls, not in-process success captures.

Three constructors with null/empty/custom/unicode messages and null/non-null inner; exact default message/HResult/native type/base type/inner identity, inherited GetBaseException, ToString without unstable stack text, Type.GetType exact/ignore-case, inherited GetObjectData selected fields. Timeout task Exception wraps TimeoutException; GetResult throws the stored same timeout exception rather than canceling. No obsolete deserialization-constructor claim.

Existing new ValueTask(waitTask), AsTask/Preserve and both awaiters observe same selected outcomes and token/exception identity without gaining ownership. Include original-fast-path and distinct-wrapper results.

privateJavaControls: Synchronous source completion during attachment; source completed between fast-path check and attach; completion before source handle publication; source/timer/token winner before each other resource publishes; constructor final completed check. Assert no retained removable action or owned timer/registration after dispatch/cleanup completes.

Each ordered pair and bounded concurrent race among source success/fault/cancel, timeout and caller cancellation; one terminal payload only, losers cannot replace it, repeat callbacks harmless. Source cancellation and caller cancellation use distinct tokens.

Source removal before detach, during concurrent add, and after detach; two waiters share source; never remove user callback/other waiter; canceled long-lived source retains no abandoned pending action.

Registration running on same/other thread during cleanup; blocked callbacks and interruption restoration; no lock held across Dispose/user callback. Test cleanup delayed by an inline user continuation without imposing a stronger-than-native immediate-cleanup contract.

Fail timer scheduling or registration after partial acquisition; injected cleanup failures; completion dispatch rejection/throwing uncaught handler; preserve winner payload and attempt all owned cleanup. Label catastrophic inability to create threads outside delivery guarantee.
First-use JVM and rejection paths do not inherit creator InheritableThreadLocal; do not claim reused workers clear arbitrary task-written locals or emulate ExecutionContext.

Exact identity and token checks across held Run queued/running/terminal states, canceled Delay asynchronous source dispatch, and mixed runtime/user callback ordering; no guessed native scheduling equivalence.
